Right, quick update from the pricing side, two minutes. We narrowed the list down from forty categories to six, and we ruled out the three where the data is too thin. The pilot is running in the south, and we are scaling it up to two more regions next month. Two open points. First, we are phasing out the old spreadsheet, so if anyone is still using it, please stop this week. Second, I brought up the sign-off delay with the commercial director on Friday and she asked me to follow up on it with finance. I will report back on Thursday. That is everything from me.

Can I give you one piece of feedback before you go? In the meeting today, you had the strongest argument in the room and you did not push back once. When the finance director said the timeline was fine, you knew it was not, and you let it go. I understand why. In a second language, disagreeing costs more energy than agreeing. But here is the thing: if you do not bring it up in the room, it comes back three weeks later as a problem with your name on it. Next time, say one sentence. Just one. I would push back on the timeline, and here is why. That is enough.

First, the team narrows the list down to six categories. Then it rules out the ones where the data is too thin. After that, it scales the pilot up to two more regions. Next, the analyst follows up on the sign-off delay with finance. Finally, he reports back to the group on Thursday.
